newsitem.title: USA: Woman pleads not guilty in Cosby extortion case.
newsitem.headline: Woman pleads not guilty in Cosby extortion case.

text.p: By Gail Appleson, U.S. Law Correspondent
A woman charged with trying to extort $40 million from entertainer Bill Cosby by claiming she was his illegitimate daughter pleaded not guilty to the charges on Thursday.

Autumn Jackson, 22, and her alleged accomplice Jose Medina, 51, both entered not guilty pleas during an arraignment in Manhattan federal court and the case was assigned to U.S. District Judge Barbara Jones.
They are charged in a three count indictment alleging they tried to obtain money from Cosby by threatening to reveal to a tabloid newpaper Jackson's claim that Cosby is her out-of-wedlock father.
They are charged with conspiracy, extortion and violating the federal law that prohibits people from engaging in interstate commerce to commit certain offences.
If convicted of all counts, they face a possible total prison term of 12 years and fines of $750,000.

Cosby has admitted to having an affair with Jackson's mother but denied fathering the girl. According to court papers, Jackson was one of many young people for whom Cosby paid educational expenses for several years.
Federal prosecutors have said there was no evidence the scheme was connected to the murder of Cosby's son Ennis, killed by a gunman in Los Angeles on Jan. 16.
"I deny the charges that have been brought against me. I would like to send my condolences to the Cosby family about Ennis's death," Jackson told reporters after the arraignment.
Her lawyer Robert Baum said evidence would show his client was Cosby's daughter.
Medina's lawyer, Neil Checkman, told reporters after the hearing his client was unaware of any extortion plot and had no intention of extorting money from the entertainer.
"He doesn't know if Autumn Jackson extorted money from Bill Cosby," Checkman said. He said his client only wanted to help Jackson get into UCLA to study film.

The indictment charges that Jackson and Medina tried to pressure Cosby into paying her by contacting Cosby's corporate sponsors and the CBS television network, which broadcasts his comedy series "Cosby."

According to the indictment, Jackson also had sent a letter to Cosby's lawyer on Jan. 16 stating "I need monies and I need monies now" and that "I don't want to do anything to harm my father in any way, if at all possible to avoid."
The indictment alleges she spoke to the lawyer on Jan. 17 and demanded $40 million. She eventually agreed to refrain from publicising her claim in exchange for $24 million.

The two defendants flew to New York on the night of Jan. 17 and met with the lawyer the next morning. They were arrested after they signed an agreement stating they would not sell Jackson's story in exchange for $24 million.
Jackson was released on bail on Jan. 28 but Medina remains in custody.
